hook: The largest known galaxy in our universe spans nearly 1.7 million light-years across.

sections.voiceover: The largest known galaxy in our universe spans nearly 1.7 million light-years across.
sections.visual_cue: Deep space wide shot of an enormous, glowing, diffuse elliptical galaxy.

sections.voiceover: On October 2, 2026, the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias published a new study analyzing the structure of IC 1101. How did researchers use 2022 Isaac Newton Telescope images to define this galaxy's physical extent?
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias logo next to the Isaac Newton Telescope.
b_roll: Institutional logo of Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias.
Exterior shot of the Isaac Newton Telescope.

sections.voiceover: However, Carlos Marrero-de la Rosa discovered the galaxy's main body is actually 520 kiloparsecs wide.
sections.visual_cue: Animated comparison showing a standard spiral galaxy shrinking next to the vast IC 1101.

sections.voiceover: The Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias confirmed the main body spans 520 kiloparsecs, or 1.7 million light-years. IC 1101 now stands as the largest galaxy ever recorded.
sections.visual_cue: A chart showing the 520 kiloparsecs value with a glowing point of light representing the galaxy.
b_roll: Data visualization of the 520 kiloparsecs measurement.

sections.voiceover: Astronomers utilized 2022 Isaac Newton Telescope data to map the true size of IC 1101.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom into the center of the galaxy, fading to black.
